summary.text: John A. Squires said AI cannot be excluded from any discussion of the future of intellectual property and described IP protection in AI, quantum, biotechnology, advanced materials, and semiconductors as essential national-security functions. In September 2026 remarks, he described the USPTO's new Emerging Technologies Office in San Francisco as a hub to advance AI use, steer AI adoption, and help U.S. companies enter the federal marketplace and export AI products. In March 2026 congressional testimony, he described agency AI efforts including the ASAP! prior-art pilot, AI agents assisting examiners on eligibility issues with a human in the loop, and AI tools used to identify fraudulent filings. He also outlined a vision of examiners deploying AI agents at scale, cited task-directed AI agents for trademark classification, and welcomed a new chief artificial intelligence officer to help aggressively modernize agency systems and workflows.

statements.text: We just opened an Emerging Technologies Office in San Francisco as part of the agency’s efforts to advance the use of AI and engage with the AI industry. This office serves as a hub to convene our stakeholders involved in AI, enabling them to work with federal officials on how best to steer AI adoption for American dominance. It will help U.S. companies gain a foothold in the federal marketplace and assist them in exporting their AI products and systems to other countries.
